title: Asset
description: Something somebody put in — a file uploaded or a page ingested from a URL — and everything a machine later said about it. The bytes never travel: what travels is where they are kept, what kind of thing they are, and the reading a pipeline made of them.

id.description: The record's own id in the system that holds it.

owner.description: The wallet, handle, or id under localIds of whoever the asset belongs to. Absent for an asset that was put in before anybody claimed it.

session.description: The id of the working session it was put in during, in the system that owns the session. Absent when it was not put in through one.

sourceType.description: How it arrived: handed over as a file, or fetched from an address.

sourceUrl.description: The address it was fetched from, when it was fetched. Kept even after ingestion, because the copy and the original drift apart.

originalFilename.description: The name the file had when it arrived. Never the name it is stored under.

contentType.description: The media type, as declared on arrival.

storageKey.description: Where the bytes sit in the store that holds them. Meaningful only to that store; a reader asks it, never resolves the key itself.

assetType.description: What kind of thing it is, which decides which pipeline reads it.

processingStatus.description: Where the pipeline stands on this asset.

processingStage.description: Which step it was on. Read together with the status, it says where a run stopped: failed at ai_enrichment is a different repair from failed at embedding_indexing. Absent before the first step runs.

aiTitle.description: A title a machine gave it, which is not the filename and not a title a person wrote.

aiDescription.description: What a machine said the asset is.

aiSummary.description: The longer reading a machine made of it.

aiTags.description: Tags a machine put on it. Free text: the vocabulary belongs to whoever enriched the asset, not to this shape.

thumbnail.description: A preview image made from the asset. A second file the asset owns, not the asset itself: it is derived, and absent until something made one.

transcriptText.description: What was said in it, for an asset that is heard rather than read.

visualSummary.description: What is seen in it, for an asset that is looked at rather than read.

embedding.description: The semantic vector of the whole asset.

metadata.description: Raw technical metadata as the extractor read it off the file — dimensions, duration, codec, whatever the format carries.

createdAt.description: When the asset was recorded, which is not when the file was made.
